items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: And those were, we were the four major students of Tio.

ctx.x: And I'm Dick Allen, and Lars Edergren is coming later. He's busy eating breakfast. Let's see, today is June the 20th, what's the date? 26th. 26th, 1972, and we're at 931 Charlotte Street, Lars Edergren's apartment. Oh, one of the things that, you remember Alan Ward, who's a friend of Mike Casimir, he was telling me that you took lessons from Tio? That's right, Lorenzo Tio. Who else would be there at the lessons at the same time? Did you meet any other musicians?
Yeah, yeah. Jimmy Noon was ahead of me. I was second, and Barney Begard and Omar Simeon. Omar Simeon, he was in Chicago. And those were, we were the four major students of Tio.

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: And Omar Simeon in Chicago, studied with Teo.

ctx.x: Did you hear much of Jimmy Noon in the old days?

I heard Jimmy Noon when I was a kid, 15 years old. As I told you, he was playing with the Young Olympia Band. In fact, we were taking lessons together with Papa Teo also. Jimmy was a couple of, about four years older than I am. And he was playing a lot of clarinet. And it was Jimmy. Bonnie came after me. Bonnie Begarde studied with Teo also. And Omar Simeon in Chicago, studied with Teo. And Teo was in Chicago. Now, Jimmy was one of the best. When he left New Orleans to join Charlie Cook's band. And when we heard…
acquaintance from him. Would you say he was a real original?
